deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the axiomatic core of Grothendieck's 1974 'topologie modérée' (tame topology) notes. On the previous page R is first an abstract set (later the real line, then a Hausdorff space). For each n there is a family C_n of subsets of R^n. These families are stable under permutations, coordinate projections, diagonal duplications of coordinates and products. Equivalently, there is a functor on finite sets: for a map alpha: I -> J of finite sets, alpha^* sends C_J into C_I, and products take C_I x C_J into C_{I disjoint union J}. A map between such sets is a C-morphism if its graph lies in C.

This page continues by defining a 'structure de C-modèle' on an abstract set E. It is a family T_n of injections u: E -> R^n (global charts) such that:
(a) some T_n is nonempty;
(b) for every u in T_m, u(E) lies in C_m;
(c) a saturation/compatibility axiom: given u in T_n and an injection v: E -> R^m, v is in T_m iff v(E) is in C_m and the transition map v u^{-1}: u(E) -> v(E) is a C-morphism.
So a C-model is a set with a maximal atlas of global embeddings whose images are C-sets, with C-morphic transition maps. It is an abstract 'C-set up to C-isomorphism', a 'modèle' in the sense later used in Esquisse §5.

Marginal alternative: the structure can instead be encoded by a set Sigma of 'C-functions' E -> R, subject to two axioms:
- some finite J in Sigma gives an injection E -> R^J with image X in C_J;
- f: E -> R lies in Sigma iff the composite X ≅ E -> R is a C-morphism.
This is a function-algebra description of the same structure, in the style of Sikorski/differential spaces. It prepares the next page, where (once the sets in C_n are compact) the structure is recovered from the sheaf of germs of C-functions, and C-spaces are defined as locally compact spaces with a subsheaf of continuous R-valued functions, locally isomorphic to C-models.

Example: any X in C_n carries a canonical C-model structure. C-morphisms between C-models are defined via charts.

Proposition 1: C-models and C-morphisms form a category with binary (hence finite) products. A morphism is an isomorphism iff it is bijective; this follows because the graph of f^{-1} is a coordinate permutation of the graph of f.

Proposition 2: the following are equivalent:
(a) some C_n contains a nonempty set;
(b) R^0 (the point) belongs to C_0, obtained by projecting a nonempty X to R^0;
(c) one-point C-models exist.
Then one-point C-models are pairwise isomorphic (the graph {(p,q)} = {p} x {q} is a product) and are final objects.

Standing assumption from now on, in the stronger form (5): R^n is the union of the members of C_n for all n. By products this reduces to n = 1. It is needed because members of C_n will be compact, so R^n itself is not in C_n.

Finally, C-parts of a C-model are defined by transport through charts, so that for X in C_n the C-parts are exactly the Y in C_n contained in X. Direct and inverse images of C-parts under morphisms are C-parts.

Purpose: to set up an abstract framework (later o-minimal-like) in which compact tame 'models' and tame spaces can be glued, independent of the specific class (semialgebraic, semianalytic, PL, ...).
errors: The framework silently needs closure of each C_n under intersection, i.e. preimages under diagonal maps. The listed axioms only give images under coordinate maps alpha^* (projections and diagonal embeddings) and products, which do not imply X ∩ Y ∈ C_n. Counterexample: let C_1 be the nondegenerate compact intervals and C_n the sets generated from them by products and coordinate maps. The diagonal of [0,1] meets [-1,0]x[0,1] in the single point (0,0), which is not in C_2. The Prop 'X,Y ∈ C_n ⇒ X∩Y ∈ C_n' on the previous page (written, struck, rewritten) is therefore an extra axiom, not a consequence.

Several statements on this page depend on that intersection axiom: composition of C-morphisms, existence of a category, the equivalent definition of C-morphisms via charts, and the stability of C-parts under inverse/direct image (computed as projections of Γ_f ∩ (X × Y'), etc.).
Minor: the example should read X ⊂ R^n, not X ∈ R^n.
Minor: 'R' here is still the abstract set R of the previous page, not yet ℝ.

ideas.what: Axiomatic families C_n ⊂ P(R^n), functorial in finite sets (stable under alpha^*) and under products and intersections, with C-morphisms defined by graphs
ideas.modern_name: a structure in the model-theoretic sense (pp/regular fragment); relational clone / co-clone; precursor of o-minimal structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal structures: van den Dries (1984), Pillay–Steinhorn (1986). Relational clones: Geiger; Bodnarchuk–Kaluzhnin–Kotov–Romov (1968-69)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (1984) describes in prose an axiomatic tame topology starting from systems of 'tame' subsets of R^n; the detailed axioms are not published

ideas.what: C-model: an abstract set with a saturated atlas of global injective charts into R^n with images in C_n and C-morphic transition maps
ideas.modern_name: definable sets up to definable bijection; affine definable spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Tame Topology and o-minimal Structures (1998), ch. 10 (definable spaces via atlases)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse uses the word 'modèles' for compact tame pieces; no detailed definition published

ideas.what: Encoding the structure by a set Sigma of admissible R-valued functions with a finite separating subfamily
ideas.modern_name: function-algebra / differential-space description; leads to the sheaf-of-tame-functions definition of tame spaces on the next page
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sikorski (differential spaces, 1967); Delfs–Knebusch (semialgebraic spaces as ringed spaces, early 1980s)

ideas.what: The category of C-models has finite products; bijective morphisms are isomorphisms; point objects exist iff some C-set is nonempty, and they are final
ideas.modern_name: basic categorical properties of a category of definable sets

ideas.what: Assumption (5) that the members of C_n cover R^n, anticipating compactness of all C-sets

missed.claim: Grothendieck's closure axioms (images under all coordinate maps alpha^* of finite sets, products, plus the needed intersections) are exactly the axioms of a relational clone (primitive-positive closed family) on R. C-models with C-morphisms then form the category of pp-definable sets, a regular-category / allegory picture. So his tame-topology axiomatics starts one level weaker than o-minimality (no complements, no unions, no finiteness condition on C_1). Requiring compact members makes the setting 'positive', unlike the Boolean o-minimal setting.
missed.quote: Il revient au même, pour tout ens. fini I, de se donner C_I ⊂ P(R^I) ... α^*(X) ∈ C_I pour X ∈ C_J
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a positive, compact-sets-only version of tame geometry (closer to 'compact definable' or PL/polyhedral categories, and to positive or coherent logic) that has not been systematically developed as a foundation for tame topology.

missed.claim: Two equivalent descriptions of tame structures (global chart atlases vs. a set Sigma of admissible functions), leading on the next page to C-spaces as locally compact spaces with a subsheaf of continuous functions locally modelled on compact C-models. The equivalence and the gluing theory are only sketched.
missed.quote: a) ∃ J ⊂ Σ, partie finie, telle que E → R^J associé soit injectif ... f ∈ Σ ssi ... est C-morphisme
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A minor point: it gives a sheaf-theoretic definition of tame spaces that anticipates Delfs–Knebusch-style ringed-space definitions, but within an axiom system independent of o-minimality.

deep.surprise_reason: These are detailed unpublished axioms behind the prose program of Esquisse §5. The constructions themselves are routine and broadly anticipated by later o-minimal and definable-space theory. Mildly interesting: the positive/compact-only axiomatics, the functorial-in-finite-sets formulation, and the missing intersection axiom.

The item labelled '5)' at top is likely 'c)', the third axiom after a) and b).
'R' should be the abstract set R (calligraphic/plain), not ℝ, at this stage.
'Ex Si n∈N, X ∈ R^n' should be 'X ⊂ R^n'.
'les C-modèles [...] 2 à 2 des objets finissent' should read approximately 'les C-modèles ponctuels sont isomorphes 2 à 2, et sont des objets finals de la catégorie des C-modèles'.
The struck item in the final condition is 'R^0 ∈ C_0', replaced by '∀ n ∈ N, R^n = ∪_{X ∈ C_n} X'.
The last line probably ends with 'Notion de C-...' followed by an illegible word ('induite' or similar).
